rationale: C25 is a strong material template. Both directives respond to an error in an earlier monument boundary description, explain that redefining the external boundaries is in the public interest, and then proclaim that lands within a metes-and-bounds description shall constitute the monument. This shared problem-specific sequence and operative machinery are substantially more concrete than the generic monument enlargement or exclusion provisions in other candidates. C23 and C07 also use a comprehensive boundary description, but neither matches the child’s correction-of-error rationale as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: a subsequent survey ... disclosed that that diagram does not accurately depict the boundaries of the monument as those boundaries are marked on the ground
shared_material.parent_excerpt: errors have been discovered in the description of the area now constituting the Sitka National Monument ... as contained in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... establishing the said monument
shared_material.explanation: Both identify an error in the monument boundaries established by an earlier directive as the predicate for corrective action.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it would be in the public interest to redefine the external boundaries of the monument in conformity with the survey
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it would be in the public interest to redefine the boundaries of the Sitka National Monument (1) to correct the above-mentioned errors of description
shared_material.explanation: The recitals share distinctive language and the same corrective-boundary purpose.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do proclaim that the lands within the following described boundaries shall constitute the Timpanogos Cave National Monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do proclaim that ... the lands now owned by the United States within the exterior boundaries of the following-described tracts of land ... shall constitute the Sitka National Monument
shared_material.explanation: The operative clause uses nearly identical machinery: proclaiming that lands within newly described exterior boundaries constitute the monument, followed by a detailed survey description.
